events.title: Constantinople Falls to the Ottomans
events.description: After a siege of about two months, Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople. The city had been the capital of the Byzantine Empire, the surviving eastern half of the Roman Empire.
events.significance: The fall ended the Byzantine Empire, which had lasted for centuries. Many historians use it to mark the end of the Middle Ages. The city became the Ottoman capital, later known as Istanbul.

events.title: Charles II Restored to the English Throne
events.description: Charles II entered London on his 30th birthday. This restored the monarchy after the period of republican rule that followed the English Civil War.
events.significance: The Restoration reestablished the Stuart monarchy. It reshaped the balance of power between Crown and Parliament in England.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Is Born
events.description: John Fitzgerald Kennedy was born in Brookline, Massachusetts. He grew up in a prominent political family.
events.significance: Kennedy became the 35th President of the United States, the youngest person elected to the office. His presidency and his assassination in 1963 left a lasting mark on American history.

events.title: Hillary and Tenzing Reach the Summit of Everest
events.description: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa mountaineer, became the first climbers confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest, the world's highest peak.
events.significance: The climb was a landmark of human endurance and teamwork. It ended a long race to reach the top of the world.
